newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares index hits high, profit taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares index hits high, profit taking seen.

text.p: The Russian Trading System (RTS) 24-share index inched up to a record close on Thursday but some shares closed mixed and traders said the market was hit by profit-taking likely to last another day or more.
The RTS index closed at 347.20, off a record 349.27 set at 0900 GMT and just up from Wednesday's record close 347.11. Total reported market volume was $54.6 million.

Natural gas monopoly Gazprom rose to $0.56 from $0.53 on about $10 million in turnover. Moscow electrical utility Mosenergo slipped to $1.509 from $1.555 on under $9 million and international telecoms provider Rostelekom fell to $4.05 from $4.34 on about $4 million.
National electricity utility UES prefs fell, like a number of pref shares, ending at $0.2000 after $0.2110 on over $3 million.
Peter Kizenko, chief equity trader at ING Baring, said the correction could last through mid-week next week but that prices would drop or be marked down no more than five percent.
"This is the first real bout of profit-taking," he said. "No one is stepping up for stock. People are just waiting."
Different traders saw selling by Russian operators and Western investors, both in limited supplies.
"People don't want to be stuck at the top holding stock," said Martin Diggle, director at Brunswick, who added traders had marked down bids rather than sold large amounts of stock.

Kirill Maltsev, institutional sales manager at Rye, Man and Gor Securities, said buying could pick up again early next week. "The correction is a relief. It can't always go up," he said of the market.

Traders saw stock available in Rostelekom and regional electrical utility Irkutskenergo, and regional shares considered undervalued showed the strongest growth. Oil producer Orenburgneft rose to $6.16 from $5.20 on February 18, when it last traded, on 100,000 shares.
